# Muscatine Mall (Muscatine, Iowa)

## Overview
Muscatine Mall is an enclosed shopping center at 1903 Park Avenue in Muscatine, Muscatine County, Iowa, United States. The complex opened in 1971 under the name Muscatine Plaza and was developed by General Management Corporation of Des Moines. Contemporary local coverage described a climate‑controlled, enclosed center with approximately 287,000 square feet of retail area and perimeter parking for about 1,900 cars. Early tenants included Montgomery Ward, Woolworth, Hy‑Vee, Walgreens, and the Plaza One & Two twin‑screen theaters. By October 1975, major advertising used the name “Muscatine Mall,” and JCPenney debuted there that month. In July 1983, Walmart opened one of its first two Iowa stores at Muscatine Mall, taking a former Woolco space. Menards opened in the former Walmart anchor in October 1998. The mall’s anchor roster and occupancy changed significantly in the 2000s and 2010s, including the opening of Elder‑Beerman in October 2003 and the closures of JCPenney in 2014 and Younkers (successor to Elder‑Beerman) in 2018. As of December 2025, the mall remains open and is used for city‑sponsored events and services, with retail occupancy reduced since the loss of several anchors. 

## Location and identification
- Street address: 1903 Park Avenue, Muscatine, IA 52761, United States. 
- Geographic coordinates: approximately 41.447619°N, 91.028397°W (Google Maps latitude/longitude at the mall’s address). 
- Jurisdiction: City of Muscatine, Muscatine County, Iowa. 
- Site context: Frontage on Park Avenue (part of the city’s north–south retail corridor); outparcels exist along Park Avenue near the mall. 

## Physical and architectural characteristics
- Configuration: Enclosed shopping mall; climate‑controlled. 
- Reported retail area at planning/announcement: approximately 287,000 square feet. 
- Parking: perimeter parking designed for about 1,900 cars. 

## Development history
- Groundbreaking: May 19, 1970. City officials and developer representatives—including Mayor Kelly Burns and Matthew Bucksbaum (president of General Management Corporation)—attended the ceremony. 
- Initial tenant lineup (leases signed by spring 1970): Woolworth, Montgomery Ward, Hy‑Vee, Walgreens, and Twin Screen Theatres (Plaza One & Two). 
- Initial openings (1970–1971):
 - Montgomery Ward opened in November 1970. 
 - Woolworth, Walgreens, Hy‑Vee, and First National Bank opened in June 1971. 
 - Formal opening of Muscatine Plaza occurred on July 15, 1971, and Plaza One & Two theaters opened July 22, 1971. 
- Name usage: By October 1975, advertisements identified the venue as “Muscatine Mall.” 
- JCPenney opening: Grand opening on October 22, 1975, with extensive advertising and a published roster of mall merchants. 
- Discount/department store changes:
 - Woolco ceased operations early in 1983; Walmart opened one of its first two Iowa stores at Muscatine Mall in July 1983 in the former Woolco space (Marshalltown Mall was the other). 
 - Menards opened in the mall’s former Walmart anchor with an unadvertised opening on October 16, 1998, and a grand opening on October 18, 1998. 
- Elder‑Beerman opening: The Bon‑Ton chain opened its first Iowa Elder‑Beerman in the south end of the mall on October 23, 2003; local coverage described a 43,500‑square‑foot store and ribbon‑cutting details. 

## Tenants and anchors timeline (selected)
- Early anchors and services:
 - Montgomery Ward (opened November 1970). 
 - Woolworth (opened June 1971; later transitioned to Woolco). 
 - Hy‑Vee and Walgreens (opened June 1971); First National Bank opened a branch at the mall entrance on June 14, 1971. 
 - Plaza One & Two theaters (opened July 22, 1971). 
- Mid‑1970s additions:
 - JCPenney opened October 22, 1975. The ad listed dozens of contemporaneous tenants (including Hy‑Vee, Walgreens, Radio Shack, Musicland, Plaza Theatres, Pizza Hut, Baskin‑Robbins, Montgomery Ward, Kinney Shoes, Gallenkamp, and others). 
- 1980s–1990s anchors:
 - Walmart opened July 1983, occupying the former Woolco space. 
 - Menards opened in October 1998 in the former Walmart anchor position. 
- 2000s–2010s changes:
 - Elder‑Beerman opened October 23, 2003; later operated under the Younkers banner before closing in 2018. 
 - JCPenney closed in 2014. 
- Leasing materials identified Slumberland Furniture among tenants as of late 2017. 

## Ownership and management
- Original developer: General Management Corporation (Des Moines), with Matthew Bucksbaum named in local coverage at the 1970 groundbreaking. 
- Subsequent transactions and records:
 - A 2006 Muscatine Journal item reported that Muscatine Mall had been purchased by a group of Quad‑City–area businessmen. 
 - City of Muscatine planning documentation references Muscatine Mall Management II, L.L.C. at 1903 Park Avenue and details relating to a Starbucks outparcel, indicating local records associated with an entity at the mall address. 
 - Municipal action related to subdivision: on May 6, 2010, the City Council agenda included approval of the final plat for “Muscatine Mall Second Addition.” 
- Current owner/manager: Publicly accessible municipal references name Muscatine Mall Management II, L.L.C. in relation to the property and its outparcels; however, comprehensive county assessor detail for all parcels of the enclosed mall has not been consolidated within the cited sources. 

## Current operational status (as of December 12, 2025)
- The mall remains open for public use. City of Muscatine departments continue to host events and programs at the mall, including:
 - Muscatine Parks and Recreation’s Elves Workshop (scheduled at Muscatine Mall on Saturday, December 13, 2025). 
 - Walking Club activities recorded at an information center in the mall’s center court. 
 - Prior events such as the Fall Festival (October 2018) and Elves Workshop (December 2018). 
- Services and access:
 - The Iowa Department of Transportation indicates Commercial Driver’s License skills and drive tests are administered at “Muscatine Plaza, 1903 Park Ave.,” with instructions to use the Iowa DOT entrance on the back side of the mall. 
- Redevelopment/zoning: The City Council’s May 6, 2010 agenda shows approval of the final plat for Muscatine Mall Second Addition. No demolition approvals or large‑scale de‑malling actions are documented in the sources cited here for 2019–2025; leasing materials and city events indicate ongoing but reduced retail usage following anchor losses. 

## Outparcels and site layout
- Outparcel formation and marketing:
 - A 0.92‑acre outparcel is listed adjacent to Muscatine Mall for retail, restaurant, or service use. 
 - Additional Park Avenue commercial lots near the mall have been marketed in recent years, reflecting continuing subdivision and outparcel activity along the corridor. 

## Economic and community role
- Public programming and civic use:
 - City‑sponsored events and programs—such as the annual Fall Festival, Elves Workshop, and the Walking Club—have used the mall’s interior corridors and center court. 
- Anchor closures and local impact:
 - In 2018, following Bon‑Ton’s bankruptcy, Younkers announced closure; local media reported the Muscatine Younkers store’s liquidation affecting approximately 45 employees, and city officials publicly addressed residents’ concerns about the mall’s future. 

## Notable events and incidents
- Government services:
 - The Iowa DOT’s Muscatine office notes CDL skills and drive tests conducted at Muscatine Plaza (1903 Park Ave.), indicating continued use of the site for state services. 
- Retail transition:
 - JCPenney confirmed the closure of its Muscatine Mall store effective May 2014 as part of a national reduction. 
 - Younkers closed in 2018 following Bon‑Ton liquidation proceedings; statewide coverage confirmed the chainwide shutdown timeline. 

## Name history
- Opening name: Muscatine Plaza (formal opening July 15, 1971). 
- Later usage: Advertisements and tenant promotions by October 1975 used “Muscatine Mall,” which remains the common name. 

## Identification summary
- Address: 1903 Park Avenue, Muscatine, IA 52761. 
- Coordinates: 41.447619°N, 91.028397°W (Google Maps at the mall address). 
- Opening: Formal opening July 15, 1971 (Plaza One & Two theaters opened July 22, 1971). 
- Developer: General Management Corporation (Des Moines); Matthew Bucksbaum participated in the 1970 groundbreaking. 
- Initial retail area: approximately 287,000 sq ft. 
- Initial anchors/major tenants: Woolworth, Montgomery Ward, Hy‑Vee, Walgreens, Plaza One & Two theaters; First National Bank opened a branch at the mall entrance June 14, 1971. 
- Parking: about 1,900 spaces, perimeter parking. 
- Subsequent anchors: JCPenney (opened October 22, 1975), Walmart (opened July 1983 in former Woolco space), Menards (opened October 16/18, 1998), Elder‑Beerman (opened October 23, 2003; later Younkers). 
- Major closures: JCPenney (2014), Younkers (2018). 
- Current status: Open as of December 2025; used for community events and state services; retail occupancy reduced since anchor departures.

David and Kevin Bills, 21, both of Council Bluffs, lowa, were being held Tuesday for investigation of murder charges after police said they confessed to stabbing Patrick Perry, 34, on Saturday. "They were basically Good Samaritans who were attacked because they were Good Samaritans," said Jim Castle, who represents Kevin Bills. Attorney Phil Cherner said the Bills were "good kids." envoy today began more talks with President Slobodan Milosevic after failing to persuade him to withdraw additional forces from Kosovo to avoid NATO Milosevic has remained defiant as envoy Richard Holbrooke sought to convince him that Washington is equally firm in demanding that he comply with U.N. resolutions or face military action. "The situation's extremely serious," Holbrooke said before today's talks began. At U.N. headquarters Tuesday, the Security Council declared that the combatants in Kosovo had not yet fully complied with U.N.

resolutions demanding a cease-fire and the withdrawal of special Serb police units from the Serb province. While the U.N. action carries no legal weight, NATO officials say they are prepared to launch airstrikes swiftly after a final decision is made. A decision is possible by the weekend, after NATO ambassadors meet Thursday. Nation Hottest costumes inspired by scandal BOSTON (AP) Forget the witches' brooms, clown noses and monster masks.

This year's most popular Halloween costume calls for a blue dress, a beret and, yes, a cigar. "We thought 'Titanic' costumes would be the big rentals, but it looks like Bill and Monica are winning the race," said Stephen LaLiberte, rental manager at Boston Costume. As impeachment hearings move forward in Washington, stores around the country are fielding requests for costumes of President Clinton, Monica Lewinsky and even Linda Tripp. "We're getting lots of requests," said Claire Olerich, owner of the Costume Gallery in Derry, N.H., noting customers are disappointed when they can't find masks bearing Ms. Lewinsky's likeness.

For the creative reveler, dressing up as a figure from the political sex scandal is easy, especially with the details provided in Independent Counsel Kenneth Starr's report and from Clinton's grand jury testimony, cast nationally last month. Jones, a disaster worker from the Muscatine Chapter of the American Red Cross, was dispatched to southern Louisiana after Tropical Storm Frances lashed the Gulf Coast on Sept. 11. As he and others were in the midst of helping locals put their lives back together by distributing aid for emergency food, clothing and shelter, Hurricane Georges paid a call on Sept.

26. "I've got to admit, it was kind of scary," Jones said. "They evacuated Red Cross personnel from New Orleans when the hurricane hit and sent us to Lake Charles, farther inland." The 14-year Red Cross veteran learned firsthand the difference in intensity between a tropical storm and a hurricane. A lot of questions were left unanswered when Ilsa Lund and Victor Laszlo fled Casablanca for Lisbon, leaving stoic saloonkeeper Rick Blaine standing on an airport tarmac in one of Hollywood's most famous final scenes. Jones has been on disaster call for the past four years with the Red Cross.

Earlier this spring, he responded to major tornadoes that wreaked havoc throughout Alabama, killing dozens. In 1994, he helped with clean-up after Tropical Storm Alberto hit the Florida Panhandle. After three weeks in stormravaged Louisiana, Jones said he was glad to be back in Iowa. "The clean-up effort down there is going very well," he said. 11.title: Penney's store in Muscatine to close in May
11.description: MUSCATINE — J.C. Penney Co. confirmed Wednesday that its store at the Muscatine Mall, a mainstay since the mall's opening in 1973, will be closed by this May.

Muscatine officials address concerns over mall, following the loss of Younkers
==============================================================================

![Image 1: Younkers storefront sign on the exterior of a retail building](https://gray-kwqc-prod.gtv-cdn.com/resizer/v2/P5FGGEPPWZJHJPCTQZ7K3JTIGQ.jpg?auth=0ddc3dad93a14e038f9d47d10c73f02823a60f25131dd46d1007267615e86dcb&width=800&height=450&smart=true)

(KWQC)

By Terrace Myles 

Published: Apr. 19, 2018 at 10:45 PM UTC

Following the announcement of all Younker's stores closing, the economic impact may be bigger in certain cities, specifically Muscatine.

The Muscatine mall has seen a few stores leave over the past few years, one of the more notable big stores to leave was JCPenney's, which closed in 2014.

Since the announcement was made that Younkers was closing too, many residents feel their options at the Muscatine mall are running thin.

"Muscatine doesn't really have that many options for buying clothes," said longtime Younker's customer, Diane Meyers. She like many other people spent time with loved ones at the retail store. "This has been a place where my mother and I spend a lot of time, we'd have coffee on Tuesday and after coffee, we'd always come out go shopping here."

But it's the convenience factor of Younkers, that's fading away quickly. "We have to go to Davenport, every time we need to get something whether it's shoe clothes we have to go all the way to Davenport or Iowa City," said Madalyn Wheeler.

That's a big economic scare for Muscatine, Muscatine Mayor Dianna Broderson says the mall has had limited options for quite some time - and that has frustrated

customers.

"Anytime you lose a big store like that the economic impact that the on a community that it serves is really felt," Broderson said. She says due to its unique location between Davenport and Iowa City, it has been a challenge to bring in big stores to the mall that people often depend on, she admits the mall does need something new to bring in customers.

"The city certainly has worked with the mall over the years to try to revitalize it and efforts continue," she said.

[Skip To Main Content](https://muscatineiowa.gov/723/Blue-Zones-Project#mainWrapTS)

Welcome to the City of Muscatine's Blue Zones Webpage!
------------------------------------------------------

On January 30, 2013, Wellmark Blue Cross and Blue Shield, Blue Zones and Healthways announced Muscatine as a Blue Zones Project™ demonstration site in Iowa. As a demonstration site, Muscatine is currently working towards Blue Zones Community™ certification.

![Image 1: Blue Zones](https://muscatineiowa.gov/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=11456)

As a demonstration site, Muscatine will receive assistance from experts to develop and implement a Blueprint for making permanent environmental, social, and policy changes that transition people into healthier behaviors that can lead to longer, happier lives.

Please join Muscatine on our path to a healthier, happier community! Please see the resources below for more information, to sign up, and to join the Blue Zones movement!

How are you helping Muscatine obtain its goal of becoming a Blue Zone demonstration site? 'Like' Muscatine's Facebook page and post your ideas, thoughts, and comments.

![Image 2: Healthiest State Initiative](https://muscatineiowa.gov/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=11457)

Muscatine Walking Club

The Walking Club is a program sponsored by the Muscatine Parks and Recreation Department.

Membership is FREE! Club members will walk at the Muscatine Mall and record their minutes at the Walking Club Information Center, located in the center court of the mall. For more information on the Walking Club, visit the [Walking Club page](https://muscatineiowa.gov/716/Walking-Club).

News Flash
==========

Muscatine News
--------------

Posted on: October 6, 2022
### [ARCHIVED] Muscatine set to host 12th annual Fall Festival

![Image 5: Fall Festival 18](https://www.muscatineiowa.gov/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=17554)

**MUSCATINE, Iowa**– The community is invited to venture out to the Muscatine Mall from 1-3 p.m. on October 15 as the Muscatine Parks and Recreation Department hosts the 12th Annual Fall Festival.

The main corridors will be filled with a variety of autumn-inspired crafts that would be perfect for home, or office, décor. A variety of games and activities that are sure to entertain the whole family will also be available throughout the Muscatine Mall during the event.

Children will have a blast creating Halloween crafts, playing games, winning prizes, and much more. Children are encouraged to wear their Halloween costumes.

Families and children of all ages are encouraged to attend this event. There is no cost to participate in the Fall Festival.

Please contact the Muscatine Parks and Recreation Department at (563) 263-0241 for more information.

Fran Donelson Administrative Secretary Harvey Allbee, Jr. City Attorney Regular Meetings In-depth Meetings 

Gregg Mandsager City Administrator January 7 & 21 July 1 & 15 January 14 July 8 February 4 & 18 August 5 & 19 February 11 (None in August) March 4 & 18 September 2 & 16 March 11 September 9 April 1 & 15 October 7 & 21 April 8 October 14 May 6 & 20 November 4 & 18 May 13 November 11 June 3 & 17 December 2 & 16 June 10 December 9 

## AGENDA THURSDAY, MAY 6, 2010 COUNCIL CHAMBERS - CITY HALL 

1 . CALL TO ORDER 2. ROLL CALL 3. INVOCATION 4. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 5. COMMUNICATIONS – CITIZENS 

A. Public Appeal of Nuisance Abatement Concerning Property Located at 517-519 Walnut Street (New Covenant Full Gospel Baptist Church) 

6. MINUTES - APPROVAL 

A. City Council Meeting – April 15, 2010 B. Joint City/County Meeting – April 22, 2010 2

7. CONSENT AGENDA 

The following items are considered to be routine by the City Council and will be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be removed from the Consent Agenda and considered in its normal sequence on the Agenda. * 9 – A-E * 13 – A-G * Bills* * Approval of attached Bills for Approval totaling $1,734,139.10, as well as receipt summaries and journal entries for November and December 2009 and January 2010, is subject to the approval of any related agenda item(s). 

8. PUBLIC HEARING 

9. PETITIONS AND COMMUNICATIONS 

A. Second reading on a new Class C Beer and Sunday Sales Permit for Highway 61 Fuels, 3103 Highway 61 North – Highway 61 Fuels LLC (pending inspections) B. First reading on a new Class C Liquor License with Sunday Sales for Tropicana NC, 1919 Grandview Avenue – Roberto Avala (pending inspections) C. Request for a new Class BW Beer/Wine with Sunday Sales for Happy Joe’s Pizza, 203 Lake Park Blvd. – Max Brewer Corp. D. Request for renewal of a Class E Liquor License with Sunday Sales Permit for Wal-Mart Supercenter #559, 3003 N. Highway 61 – Wal-Mart Stores Inc. E. Request for renewal of a Class C Liquor License with Sunday Sales and Outdoor Service for Mike’s Hilltop Tap, 929 Lucas Street – Mike’s Hilltop Inc. F. Request Approval for Use of City Property for St. Mary’s/St. Mathias Religious Procession Presented for City Council’s consideration is a request from the St. Mary’s/St. Mathias Parish to hold a religious procession. The procession, which will take place on June 6, 2010 from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., will travel down 8 th Street to Iowa Avenue travel up 5 th Street to Pine Street and end back on 8 th Street. The event is expected to have approximately 400 participants. Is there a motion to approve the request as submitted? 3G. Request Approval for Use of City Property for 4 th of July Activities Presented for City Council’s consideration is a request from the Greater Muscatine Chamber of Commerce and Industry for the use of city property for the annual 4 th of July fireworks and parade. The fireworks celebration will begin at dusk on Sunday, July 4, 2010. The parade will take place earlier that day. Staging will begin at 3 p.m. at Fulliam and Iowa with a 5 p.m. start time. It will follow Iowa Avenue to 2 nd Street, travel up Walnut to 5 th Street, ending in front of the Public Safety Building. Is there a motion to approve the request as submitted? H. Update on Recent Police Activities 

10. FROM THE MAYOR 

A. Proclamation Declaring May 17-21, 2010 as “Bike to Work Week” B. Proclamation Declaring May 28-29, 2010 as “Poppy Days” C. Proclamation Declaring May 9-15, 2010 as “Peace Officers’ Memorial Week” and May 12, 2010 as “Peace Officers’ Memorial Day” D. Proclamation Declaring May 9-15, 2010 as “National Nursing Home Week” Is there a motion to adopt the proclamations as submitted? 

11. FROM THE PLANNING AND ZONING COMMISSION 

A. Resolution Approving the Final Plat of the Muscatine Mall Second Addition in the City of Muscatine Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution approving the final plat for the Muscatine Mall Second Addition in the City of Muscatine. City staff has been working with representatives of the Muscatine Mall, owners of 29.43 acres of real estate located at 1903 Park Avenue, to create a single-lot 5.484 acre subdivision for residential development. If approved, the owner’s intend to develop a mixture of townhouses and apartments on this lot. The Planning and Zoning Commission is recommending the approval of the final plat. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? 4

12. FROM THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR 

A. Resolution Awarding the Sale of General Obligation Corporate Purpose Bonds Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution awarding the sale of General Obligation Corporate Purpose Bonds. This bond issue will provide funding for $1,535,000 of Downtown TIF area improvements with the remaining $5,890,000 of the bond proceeds used for various street, parks, public building, airport, and trail projects. The city’s financial advisor will be reviewing the bids received and making a recommendation for the award of this issue. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? B. First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Title 3 Public Way and Property Chapter 9 Street Obstruction Presented for City Council’s consideration is the first reading of an ordinance amending Title 3 Public Way and Property Chapter 9 Street Obstruction. At the April 8, 2010 In-Depth meeting this matter was reviewed with City Council. The proposed ordinance amendment will address snow removal and its placement on city streets and public right-of-ways. The Police Department will enforce the ordinance assisted by Public Works staff who will identify the offenders. Is there a motion to approve the first reading of the ordinance as submitted? C. First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Title 7 Police Regulations Chapter 18 Snow Emergency Regulations Presented for City Council’s consideration is the first reading of an ordinance amending Title 7 Police Regulations Chapter 18 Snow Emergency Regulations. The proposed ordinance amendment will designate staff members who will work with the Police Department in enforcement of the ordinance. Is there a motion to approve the first reading of the ordinance as submitted? D. Resolution Setting a Public Hearing on a Development Agreement with Heinz Company, Including Tax Increment Payments in an Amount Not to Exceed $375,000 Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution setting a public hearing on a development agreement with Heinz Company, including tax increment payments in an amount not to exceed $375,000. In January 2010 City Council adopted an Urban Renewal Plan for the 2010 Industrial Urban Renewal Area to facilitate the use of tax increment financing incentives in support of the improvements that are being made at the Heinz facility. Prior to approval of the development agreement, a public hearing is required. The public hearing has been set for Thursday, May 20, 2010, at 7 p.m. 5Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? E. Resolution Accepting Low Bid for a Snow Removal Tractor for the Municipal Airport Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution accepting the low bid for a snow removal tractor for the municipal airport. Bids were solicited for this purchase with the only bid from Elder Implement Company in the amount of $122,727.68. The cost estimate for this purchase, which includes acquisition, engineering, and bid preparation, was $136,250. The purchase is 95% federally funded with a 5% local share. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? F. Resolution Setting Public Hearing on the Plans, Specifications, Form of Contract, Cost Estimate and Setting Bid Opening Date for the Hangar Access Road at the Airport Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution setting a public hearing on the plans, specifications, form of contract, cost estimate and setting the bid opening date for the hangar access road at the airport. On July 14, 2009, the city was awarded funding by the Iowa Department of Transportation’s Division Aviation for the construction of a hangar access road at the airport. The construction of this access road will allow access to HNI Hangar #2, provide road access for future hangar development, and serve the area intended for the construction of an armory facility on the southeast corner of the airport property. The project estimate of $98,528 will be cost shared at 85% state funding and 15% local funding. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? G. Resolution Releasing a Real Estate Mortgage Under the 2003 CDBG Owner-Occupied Residential Rehabilitation Program Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution releasing a real estate mortgage under the 2003 CDBG Owner-Occupied Residential Rehabilitation Program for property located at 615 E. 8 th Street. The property owner received the maximum $24,999 funding assistance through a five-year forgivable loan with the entire debt now forgiven. This is the fifth of 11 mortgages that eventually are expected to be released under the 2003 program. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? H. Resolution Setting a Public Hearing on the Clay Street Bridge Rehabilitation Project Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution setting a public hearing on the Clay Street Bridge Rehabilitation Project. During the Clay Street Reconstruction 6Project that took place in 2009, it was found the concrete deck was severely deteriorated. Clay Street is a truck route and carries other heavy traffic including city maintenance vehicles; therefore, immediate repair is warranted to serve businesses who utilize the street. Prior to moving forward on this project, a public hearing is required. The public hearing has been set for Thursday, May 20, 2010, at 7 p.m. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? I. Resolution Setting a Public Hearing on the 2010 Curb and Gutter and Street Maintenance Program Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution setting a public hearing on the 2010 Curb and Gutter and Street Maintenance Program. This year’s project will focus on full-depth patching of Lowe Street from Bridgeman to Longhurst Street and Longhurst Lane from Lowe Street to the cul-de-sac. There will be some curb repair on these streets as well on Newell Avenue. This work must be done prior to the asphalt overlay work. Prior to moving forward on this project, a public hearing is required. This public hearing will be held on Thursday, May 20, 2010, at 7 p.m. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? J. Resolution Amending and Approving the Official Pay Plan for Non-Union Employees Effective May 10, 2010 Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution amending and approving the official pay plan for non-union employees effective May 10, 2010. This action will add the Assistant WPCP Director/Environmental Coordinator position to the non-union pay plan. This position was approved by City Council during its budget review sessions. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? K. Resolution Supporting a Local Housing Trust Fund for Muscatine County Presented for City Council’s consideration s a resolution supporting a Local Housing Trust Fund (LHTF) for Muscatine County. The Iowa Finance Authority awards grants to approved LHTFs throughout the State of Iowa. During the past year, the Housing Department, Muscatine County Community Service Program, MCSA and United Way have been involved in a planning process that could allow a LHTF to be established for residents in Muscatine County. If established, the mission of LHTF would be to provide resources to sustain and expand affordable housing opportunities for low-income families of Muscatine County. It is staff’s recommendation City Council support the development of a LHTF for Muscatine County in the form of a partnership with the Scott County Housing Council LHTF. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? 7L. Resolution Setting a Public Hearing on Amendment #2 to the 2009/2010 City Budget Presented for City Council’s consideration is a resolution setting a public hearing on Amendment #2 to the 2009/2010 city budget. Each year the city takes two separate actions to amend the current fiscal year budget. The first amendment to the 2009/2010 budget took place on March 11, 2010 and amended the budget to the revised estimate level established during the budget review sessions. The second opportunity comes in May and/or June prior to the end of the fiscal year. Information has been solicited from the various departments that propose to make adjustments in either expenditures or revenues within their departments. Prior to any formal action by City Council, a public hearing is required. The public hearing will be held on Thursday, May 20, 2010, at 7 p.m. Is there a motion to adopt the resolution as submitted? M. Request to Approve the Amended City of Muscatine Snow and Ice Control Policy Presented for City Council’s consideration is a request to approve the amended City of Muscatine Snow and Ice Control Policy. This policy was adopted more than 25 years ago to set a standard of addressing snow and ice related storms. The city’s methodology has been altered when addressing snow and ice control. Tonight’s action would amend the policy to reflect current operations. Is there a motion to approve the request as submitted? N. Request to Approve 28E Agreement with the City of Fruitland for Refuse Collection Services Presented for City Council’s consideration is a request to approve the 28E agreement with the City of Fruitland for refuse collection services. In June 2009 the city entered into an agreement with the City of Fruitland to provide refuse and recycling collection services. That contract expires on June 30, 2010, and the City of Fruitland is requesting approval of another contract beginning July 1, 2010 and ending June 30, 2011. Is there a motion to approve the request as submitted? 8O. Request to Approve Height Exception from U.S. Cellular for a Cell Tower on the Muscatine Community Y Property Presented for City Council’s consideration is a request to approve a height exception from U.S. Cellular for a cell tower on the Muscatine Community Y property located at 1823 Logan Street. The city has received a request from U.S. Cellular to allow the construction of a 120’ monopole communications tower at this location. This request has been reviewed by the Site Plan Review Committee and now requires approval by City Council. It is staff’s recommendation this request be approved. Is there a motion to approve the request as submitted? 

13. COMMUNICATIONS - RECEIVE AND FILE 

A. Muscatine County Board of Supervisors – April 5, 12 & 19, 2010 B. Senior Resources – March 23, 2010 C. Board of Water, Electric, and Communications Trustees – March 30, 2010 D. MP&W Communications Utility – March 2010 E. MP&W Electric Utility – March 2010 F. MP&W Water Utility – March 2010 

14. APPROVAL OF BILLS 

It is recommended bills totaling $1,734,139.10, as well as receipt summaries and journal entries for November and December 2009 and January 2010, be approved and that the City Council authorize the Mayor and City Clerk to issue warrants for the same. It should be noted that this listing is subject to the approval of any related agenda item(s). 

15. COMMUNICATIONS - COUNCIL MEMBERS 

16. OTHER BUSINESS 

17. ADJOURNMENT

[![Image 23: Facebook](https://www.wqad.com/assets/shared-images/icons/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=228741701473378&display=popup&href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wqad.com%2Farticle%2Fnews%2Flocal%2Fjc-penney-to-close-33-stores-and-lay-off-thousands%2F526-4d7c7ded-e7e2-49de-b9c5-e50f8f98809e&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wqad.com%2Farticle%2Fnews%2Flocal%2Fjc-penney-to-close-33-stores-and-lay-off-thousands%2F526-4d7c7ded-e7e2-49de-b9c5-e50f8f98809e)

A location in Muscatine, Iowa, is among dozens of JC Penney stores that will close as the company makes financial changes.

JC Penney announced Wednesday, January 15, 2014, that it would close 33 stores in 20 states and lay off approximately 2,000 employees.

"These actions are expected to result in an annual cost savings of approximately $65 million, beginning in 2014," the company said [in a press release](http://ir.jcpenney.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=70528&p=irol-newsCompanyArticle&ID=1891155&highlight=).

[The release](http://ir.jcpenney.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=70528&p=irol-newsCompanyArticle&ID=1891155&highlight=) says JC Penney will close “underperforming stores across the country in order to focus on its resources on the company’s highest potential growth opportunities.”

The store at the Muscatine Mall was the only Iowa location on the list of stores to be closed as part of this action.  In Illinois, JC Penney planned to close its Stratford Square Mall store in Bloomingdale and its Hickory Point store in Forsyth.

Shoppers in Muscatine were disappointed by the news Wednesday. Many said they would now be more likely to shop in the Quad Cities than at their local mall.

"There's nothing exciting here, nothing. I would rather go out of town to go shopping," said Trinity Trafelet. "I only come here to go to JC Penney's, and that's rarely ever."

Diamond Dave's restaurant opened just three months ago in the Muscatine Mall, and co-owner Enrique Minjares said he was "shocked" by the closure.

"J.C. Penney usually brings a lot of business from out of town. They go and do shopping, and then they stop here for drinks. So, that's going to affect us, for sure," said Minjares.

Wisconsin, though, was perhaps hit hardest by the announcement, as five JC Penney stores will close in that state.

The company forecast the closures would save JC Penney about $65 million beginning in 2014.

“Eligible associates who do not remain with the Company will receive separation benefits packages. Meanwhile, the Company is continuing its plans to open a new store location later this year at the Gateway II development in Brooklyn, N.Y.,” the statement said.

The stores on the list were expected to be closed by early May 2014.

End of an era: Younkers stores to close by end of summer or sooner
==================================================================

 [![Image 1: Portrait of Patt Johnson](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/gcdn/-mm-/a85ca5443db9cad1c87e8e3f4d636214a2d2ebcc/c=0-0-400-400/local/-/media/2015/01/11/IAGroup/DesMoines/635565941878903514-Patt-Johnson-Square.jpg?width=48&height=48&fit=crop&format=pjpg&auto=webp) Patt Johnson](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/staff/2646680001/patt-johnson/)

The Des Moines Register

April 18, 2018Updated April 19, 2018, 9:04 a.m. CT

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?display=popup&app_id=169766623060429&href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.desmoinesregister.com%2Fstory%2Fmoney%2Fbusiness%2F2018%2F04%2F18%2Fyounkers-bon-ton-close-sale-bankruptcy-stores-iowa-shopping-retail-amazon-going-out-business%2F528308002%2F)[](https://x.com/intent/post?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.desmoinesregister.com%2Fstory%2Fmoney%2Fbusiness%2F2018%2F04%2F18%2Fyounkers-bon-ton-close-sale-bankruptcy-stores-iowa-shopping-retail-amazon-going-out-business%2F528308002%2F&text=End%20of%20an%20era%3A%20Younkers%20stores%20to%20close%20by%20end%20of%20summer%20or%20sooner&via=DMRegister)[](mailto:?subject=End%20of%20an%20era%3A%20Younkers%20stores%20to%20close%20by%20end%20of%20summer%20or%20sooner%20-%20from%20The%20Des%20Moines%20Register&body=End%20of%20an%20era%3A%20Younkers%20stores%20to%20close%20by%20end%20of%20summer%20or%20sooner%0A%0AYounkers%20stores%20will%20close%20after%20a%20judge%20approves%20the%20sale%20of%20parent%20company%20Bon-Ton%20to%20a%20liquidation%20company%20for%20%24775.5%20million.%0A%0ACheck%20out%20this%20story%20on%20desmoinesregister.com%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.desmoinesregister.com%2Fstory%2Fmoney%2Fbusiness%2F2018%2F04%2F18%2Fyounkers-bon-ton-close-sale-bankruptcy-stores-iowa-shopping-retail-amazon-going-out-business%2F528308002%2F)

Keep Watching

One of the most recognizable names in Iowa retail will be gone by the end of the summer.

The sale of Younkers' parent company Bon-Ton Stores Inc. to a liquidation company awaits a Delaware bankruptcy judge's signature to finalize the deal.

![Image 2: Rhonda Thomas of Des Moines shops for some good deals at Younkers at Southridge Mall in Des Moines in 2012.](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/money/business/2018/04/18/younkers-bon-ton-close-sale-bankruptcy-stores-iowa-shopping-retail-amazon-going-out-business/528308002/)

Under the agreement, the company's 256 stores, including 49 Younkers stores, will close by the end of August and assets, including store merchandise and property, will be sold.

USA TODAY Shopping: [Shop sales in tech, home, fashion, beauty & more curated by our editors.](https://www.usatoday.com/shopping/)

![Image 3: Outside the Younkers store in Valley West Mall on Wednesday, April 18, 2018, in West Des Moines. Bon-Ton Stores Inc., the owner of Younkers has filed for bankruptcy which could lead to the closure of the company's 250 stores, including 15 in Iowa.](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/money/business/2018/04/18/younkers-bon-ton-close-sale-bankruptcy-stores-iowa-shopping-retail-amazon-going-out-business/528308002/)

It's the end of an era for Iowa shoppers used to seeing the Younkers name on shopping malls across the state. The company was founded in Keokuk in 1856 and grew to become the largest department store chain in Iowa and Nebraska.

There are 17 Younkers stores remaining in Iowa that will close with the liquidation.

**More:** [What Iowa shoppers are saying about the Younkers closure on social media](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/local/2018/04/18/younkers-close-iowa-memories-thoughts-twitter-facebook-social-media-posts/527739002/)

Great American Group and Tiger Capital Group reportedly reached an agreement to purchase Bon-Ton for $775.5 million on Tuesday, according to the website Reorg Research.

A hearing was scheduled for Wednesday afternoon for the judge to sign off on the agreement terms, which would close all Bon-Ton stores by Aug. 31.

[![Image 4](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/money/business/2018/04/18/younkers-bon-ton-close-sale-bankruptcy-stores-iowa-shopping-retail-amazon-going-out-business/528308002/)](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/picture-gallery/news/local/des-moines/2014/03/29/the-younkers-building-the-downtown-store-through-the-years/7050159/)According to bankruptcy filings, Bon-Ton operates stores in 23 states that employ about 23,000 people. The company owns 22 locations and leases the remaining.

It operates stores under the names Younkers, Bon-Ton, Carson Pirie, Herberger's, Bergner's, Boston Store and Elder-Beerman.

Bon-Ton is the latest in a string of big-box retailers to close.

Toys R Us is closing all its stores while Macy's, Sears and Kmart are cutting back significantly on locations. Retailers have blamed online shopping in part on the demise of the brick and mortar stores.

► More: [Younkers stores in Iowa could close as company heads to liquidation](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/money/business/2018/04/17/younkers-close-bon-ton-bankruptcy-des-moines-iowa-stores-out-business-liquidation/523625002/)

► More: [Younkers' parent company has filed for bankruptcy. What will happen to Des Moines stores?](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/money/business/2018/02/05/younkers-parent-company-bankruptcy-des-moines-stores-close/307279002/)

Locally, Younkers has stores at four Des Moines-area malls, including Merle Hay Mall, Southridge, Jordan Creek Town Center and Valley West Mall. How soon those locations could close has not yet been announced.

![Image 5: There are 17 Younkers stores in Iowa that will close by the end of the summer.](https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/money/business/2018/04/18/younkers-bon-ton-close-sale-bankruptcy-stores-iowa-shopping-retail-amazon-going-out-business/528308002/)

And what does the Bon-Ton demise portend for department stores in general?

"This is not the end of department stores," said Richard Hurd, a longtime retail developer in the Des Moines area. "I think we'll see a continuation of a pruning, not an end. Some strong players in the high-end and middle- to high-end category will continue to thrive and be dominate."

But echoing the sentiments of hundreds of longtime Younkers shoppers, Hurd said closing the stores is a loss for the community.

"This is a big loss," he said. "It's part of our heritage here in Iowa. Anyone in their late 20s, early 30s and older, I think, has a warm place in their heart for Younkers."

The liquidation company's sale agreement outlines some of the rules for the liquidation sale, including:

*   Returns to be made 10 days from the start of the sale.
*   Gift cards and credits to be used within 10 days from the sale start.
*   Liquidation company can add outside items to the sale if they are similar to the stores' merchandise.
*   The company will continue online sales for four weeks.
*   Some current employees may be kept on to work at the liquidation sale.

Walking Club
============

What is the Walking Club?

The Walking Club is a program sponsored by the Muscatine Parks and Recreation Department. Membership is FREE! Club members will walk and then record their minutes at the Walking Club Information Center, located in the center court of the Muscatine Mall.

Member Benefits

The most important benefit is committing to a healthier lifestyle by being active! In addition, weekly drawings will be held for incentive prizes for those members who have walked and recorded minutes for that week. Winners will be notified of their prize on the poster at the mall.

When can I walk?

The Muscatine Mall hours are as follows:

*   Monday - Saturday: 8 am - 8 pm
*   Sunday: 12 pm - 5 pm

Or you can walk anytime and anywhere you’d like!

How long will it take us to walk for one million minutes?
---------------------------------------------------------

Join us in the Million Minute Challenge! Submit your weekly minutes walked to be entered to win incentive prizes over the phone at (563) 263-0241 or via email to [parksoffice@muscatineiowa.gov](mailto:parksoffice@muscatineiowa.gov). How long will it take our group to reach one million minutes walked?

How Do I Register?

Please create an account on our new platform [RecDesk](https://muscatineiowa.recdesk.com/Community/Home) to be included in all of our news release and to receive updates about the Muscatine Walking Club.

For More Information...
-----------------------

26.content:
Section of The Post The Muscatine Journal-July 18, 1990 Page 3 CELEBRATES 120 YEARS! ST NATIONAL BANK C.R. Musser assumed the position of Chairman of the Board of Muscatine Bank and Trust Company in 1940 and W.E. Downer was named president. From 1939 to 1945 the nation experienced an economic boom and a drastic decrease in unemployment as World War II was waged. The bank's assets tripled during this war time boom, increasing to nearly $15,000,000.

Over the next 15 years, the nation went through which numerous economic changes effected the American lifestyle, savings, and buying power. In 1949 the minimum wage jumped from to an hour. By 1960, the average American's per capita income was $2,218 a year. During this period the Muscatine Bank and Trust Company continued to prosper, as did the Muscatine community. In response to its increased patronage and in an attempt to offer its customers maximum convenience, Muscatine Bank and Trust opened its first' Branch in 1961.

This was the first of its kind for Muscatine. The Drive-In, which is located at the corner of Third and Cedar Streets, is still in operation today. In 1958 following W.E. Downer's presidency, B.L. McKee was named to the post.

Upon his death in 1961, F.W. Allen held the office of president until 1963, when George A. Shepley was appointed president of Muscatine Bank and Trust Company, Shepley would remain in the position for over 25 years. In 1964, under G.A. Shepley's supervision, the main bank was again renovated to keep pace with customer needs and to provide a more pleasant banking atmosphere.

Muscatine Bank and Trust Company, still a state bank, became chartered as a national bank in 1966 and changed to its present name of First National Bank of Muscatine. Under this name the bank has experienced tremendous growth and continued its long-standing tradition of community support. In order to provide our customers with greater convenience, a second branch was built in 1971. Located at the entrance of the Muscatine Mall, the Plaza opened June 14, 1971. At that time the bank's assets exceeded $40,000,000.

In 1978 a new main bank building was constructed at 300 East Second Street. The three story brick building provided increased convenience, the latest in banking equipment, and an attractive facility from which to serve the customers in the coming decades. As First National Bank entered the 1980's, its assets surpassed $100,000,000. In May 1981, the bank further expanded it's drive-up service by opening a third branch, Southside, at 608 Grandview Avenue. The final drive-in addition was completed in 1984 when the Plaza drive-in was relocated from the main Mall to a freestanding building in the adjacent lot.

Also in 1984, a bank holding company, Iowa First Bancshares was formed by the stockholders of First National Bank of Muscatine. This was done to facilitate the purchase of First National Bank in Fairfield, Iowa. This purchase was initiated to further strengthen and increase profitability to bank 'stockholders. In 1989, George A. Shepley relinquished his position as president, retaining his seat as Chairman of the Board, and Paul N.

Payne was elected to his present position as President and C.E.O. First National Bank's past has been directed by progressive and growth-oriented attitudes. During its 120 years in operation, First National Bank, under various names and personnel, has continuously supported the community it was built from and will enthusiastically follow this tradition into the twentyfirst century. 120 years ago, five people began with $25,000 in assets; today, 43,830 days later, over 90 people actively work for the safety and earning power of over $177,000,000 in assets. If it is true that there is safety in numbers, then this year we celebrate 120 good reasons to bank with First National Bank of Muscatine.

HOME FIRST NATIONAL BANK Plaza Office upon completion in 1971 El fat First National Bank of Muscatine, Mall Drive-In Southside Office, 608 Grandview, upon completion in 1981 The newly constructed Main Bank Building, Second and Cedar, 1978.
